decisions.statement: A tree is named by the whole hash of the commit it holds.
What a caller says is read as a commit by git rather than taken as a hash.
A name git reads as no commit is the caller's mistake.
A tree already laid down is run again rather than laid down twice.
A tree counts as laid down only once the whole of it is there.
A lay-down that failed leaves nothing behind for the next one to find.
The packages are the checkout's own, reached from the tree by one link each, caches apart.
The package named for this repository points at the tree rather than the checkout.
A cache a package folder hides is left out, so each tree builds its own.
Every file the commit holds is laid down refusing a write, so the tree is read alone.
A folder stays open to writing, so a build and a cache are made inside the tree.

definition: the tree a dev server runs, laid down from the commit it is named by
